title: Sandboxed iframes
description: Sandboxed iframes run untrusted code safely: the sandbox attribute strips permissions (no same-origin, no scripts — then re-adds only what's needed), and the code runs in a separate origin. allow-scripts without allow-same-origin is the sweet spot: scripts run but can't touch the parent. This is the foundation every browser playground stands on.
mechanism: <iframe sandbox='allow-scripts'>: scripts yes, same-origin no, forms/popups only if allowed. Separate origin per playground. CSP on top.
demo:
print('<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src="/playground/abc123">')
print('permissions: scripts YES | same-origin NO | parent DOM: UNREACHABLE')
print('add allow-modals/allow-popups only if the feature needs them')
print('separate origin per playground + CSP headers on top')
print('the browser is the sandbox: use it, do not reimplement it')

title: Live reload
description: Live reload re-runs the playground on every edit: debounce the keystrokes (~500ms), rebuild, and swap the iframe content. State preservation (keep the app's state across reloads) is the advanced version — naive reload loses it. The reload must be fast (<1s) or the feedback loop breaks; show a subtle indicator while rebuilding.
mechanism: Edit -> debounce -> rebuild -> iframe.srcdoc swap (or postMessage). State: serialize/restore hooks for advanced. Indicator during rebuild.
demo:
import time

last_edit, state = 0, {}

def on_edit(code):
    global last_edit
    last_edit = time.time()
    return 'debouncing...'

def tick():  # 500ms after last edit: rebuild
    if time.time() - last_edit > 0.5:
        return 'REBUILT in 320ms (iframe swapped; state kept via hooks)'
    return 'waiting'

print(on_edit('x = 1'))
time.sleep(0.6)
print(tick())
print('debounce ~500ms; rebuild <1s; state hooks for the advanced version')

title: Console capture
description: Console capture shows the playground's logs beside the code: the iframe's console methods are overridden to postMessage each call to the parent, which renders them in the console panel. Errors include stacks (mapped through sourcemaps). The panel supports levels (log/warn/error), filtering, and clearing — a real console, not a text dump.
mechanism: Override console.* in the iframe -> postMessage({level, args}) -> parent renders. Error stacks via window.onerror. Sourcemaps for real line numbers.
demo:
# iframe: console.log -> postMessage -> parent renders
messages = []

def iframe_log(level, *args):  # runs INSIDE the iframe (overridden console)
    messages.append({'level': level, 'args': [str(a) for a in args]})

def parent_render():  # runs in the PARENT (console panel)
    for m in messages:
        print('[%s] %s' % (m['level'].upper(), ' '.join(m['args'])))

iframe_log('log', 'x =', 42)
iframe_log('warn', 'deprecated')
iframe_log('error', 'boom')
parent_render()
print('levels + filter + clear; stacks via window.onerror + sourcemaps')

title: Multi-file playgrounds
description: Multi-file playgrounds go beyond one editor: files in tabs, imports between them, and a bundler (esbuild-wasm in the browser) assembling the result. The file tree is the project model; the bundler resolves the imports; the output runs in the sandbox. It is a real IDE, miniature — and the architecture (files -> bundle -> run) scales to full projects.
mechanism: Virtual FS (files in memory) -> bundler (esbuild-wasm) -> bundle -> sandboxed iframe. Imports resolved within the project; npm via CDN (esm.sh).

title: Error overlays
description: Error overlays show playground errors where the user looks: the error renders over the preview with the message, the file/line, and a click-to-jump. Runtime errors come from window.onerror; compile errors from the bundler. The overlay dismisses on the next successful build. It turns 'blank page, what happened' into 'here is exactly what broke'.
mechanism: window.onerror + bundler errors -> overlay component with message/file/line -> click jumps to the editor location. Dismiss on successful rebuild.
demo:
# error overlay: message + location + click-to-jump, over the preview
error = {'message': 'x is not defined', 'file': 'main.js', 'line': 3,
         'stack': 'at main (main.js:3:5)'}

def show_overlay(e):
    print('+' + '-' * 46 + '+')
    print('| ERROR in %-36s |' % (e['file'] + ':' + str(e['line'])))
    print('| %-44s |' % e['message'])
    print('| click -> jump to editor location                |')
    print('+' + '-' * 46 + '+')

show_overlay(error)
print('dismisses on next successful build (not manually)')

title: Hot reload
description: Hot reload updates the running app without losing state: the bundler sends the changed module, the runtime swaps it (HMR protocol), and the app continues. For playgrounds this means the demo keeps its state while the code changes — the feedback loop tightens from seconds to milliseconds. State that can't hot-swap falls back to full reload.
mechanism: HMR: bundler tracks module graph -> changed module -> runtime accept handler -> swap. No handler = full reload. State preserved by the app's own design.

title: Collaborative playgrounds
description: Collaborative playgrounds let multiple cursors edit together: CRDTs (Yjs) sync the documents, presence shows who is where, and execution is per-user (my run doesn't disturb yours) or shared. The architecture is the collaboration database's problem; the playground adds shared cursors, follow mode, and per-user consoles.
mechanism: Yjs CRDT per file -> presence (cursors, selections) -> execution sandboxed per user (or shared toggle). Follow mode for teaching.

title: Playground persistence
description: Playground persistence saves the work: autosave to the account (debounced), shareable URLs (the code in the URL or behind an id), forks (copy to your account), and version history. Anonymous playgrounds persist in localStorage; signed-in syncs to the cloud. The URL is the save file — open it anywhere, the code is there.
mechanism: Debounced autosave; URL encodings (short ids server-side, or compressed in hash); forks; history per playground. Anonymous -> localStorage; account -> cloud.
demo:
import base64, zlib, json

code = {'files': {'main.py': 'print("hi")'}}
# shareable URL: compressed code in the hash (small) or id server-side
packed = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(zlib.compress(json.dumps(code).encode())).decode()
url = 'https://play.example/#' + packed
print('share URL len:', len(url))
# restore
restored = json.loads(zlib.decompress(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(packed)))
print('restored:', restored['files'])
print('forks: copy to your account; history per playground')

title: Playground theming
description: Playground theming covers the editor (syntax theme), the UI chrome (dark/light), and the preview (the user's page, unthemed). Editor themes are separate from app themes — a dark UI with a light editor is legitimate. The theme picker previews live. Accessibility: the editor theme meets contrast minimums for code readability.
mechanism: Editor theme (Monaco/CodeMirror themes) + UI theme (tokens) independent. Preview unthemed (user's content). Live preview in the picker.

title: Playground accessibility
description: Playgrounds must be keyboard-usable: the editor is (Monaco is accessible), the run button is reachable, results are announced, and the console is navigable. Screen reader users get the code, the output, and the errors — in that order. The canvas preview gets a text alternative (the console output often serves).
mechanism: Accessible editor (Monaco); labeled controls; live regions for output/errors; console as the text alternative for visual output.

title: Playground performance
description: Playground performance is rebuild + run time: the bundler must be fast (esbuild-wasm, incremental), the iframe swap cheap, and large outputs virtualized (a million console lines can't all render). Web Workers move heavy work (bundling, execution for some languages) off the UI thread. Budget: edit -> result in under 1s.
mechanism: Incremental bundling; worker threads for build/run; virtualized console; iframe reuse (not recreate). Measure edit-to-result.

title: Playground security
description: Playground security is layered: sandboxed iframes (the browser), CSP headers (no inline, no external), execution limits (time, memory, network), origin isolation (per-playground origins), and abuse controls (rate limits, no crypto mining). The threat model assumes malicious code — because users paste it. Defense in depth, not one wall.
mechanism: sandbox attr + CSP + limits (timeout, memory, no net) + isolated origins + rate limits + monitoring. Each layer independent.
demo:
print('PLAYGROUND SECURITY LAYERS')
print('1. iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" (no same-origin: parent unreachable)')
print('2. CSP: default-src none; script-src self (no inline, no external)')
print('3. limits: 5s CPU, 256MB, no network (configurable)')
print('4. origin per playground (storage isolated)')
print('5. abuse: rate limits, mining detection, reporting')

title: Embedding playgrounds
description: Embedding playgrounds puts live code in docs and blogs: an iframe embed with the code preloaded, sized to the content, theme-matched to the page. The embed API controls which UI shows (editor only? console?); the host page communicates via postMessage (run this code, get the result). Docs with runnable examples teach 10x better.

title: Execution limits
description: Execution limits keep playgrounds safe and fair: CPU time (kill infinite loops), memory (cap the heap), output size (truncate runaway logs), network (deny by default), and wall time. The limits are communicated ('killed after 5s CPU') not mysterious. Fair scheduling shares runners across users; abuse detection handles the miners.
mechanism: Timeouts (wall + CPU); memory caps; output truncation; no network; fair queue. Clear messages on limit hits ('infinite loop? killed at 5s').
demo:
import signal

LIMIT_S = 2

def handler(signum, frame):
    raise TimeoutError('killed after %ds CPU (infinite loop?)' % LIMIT_S)

signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, handler)
signal.alarm(LIMIT_S)
try:
    total = 0
    while True:  # malicious/buggy: infinite loop
        total += 1
except TimeoutError as e:
    print(e)
finally:
    signal.alarm(0)
print('limits: CPU, memory, output size, network=deny; communicated, not mysterious')

title: Playground versioning
description: Playground versioning tracks the code's history: every run snapshots (or explicit saves version), the history shows diffs, and any version restores. For teaching, versions are the lesson's steps. The storage is content-addressed (this lane's CAS database) — identical code versions dedup automatically.
mechanism: Snapshot per save/run -> version list with diffs -> restore any. CAS storage (dedup). Teaching: versions as lesson steps.
demo:
import hashlib

versions, store = [], {}

def save(code):
    h = hashlib.sha256(code.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    store.setdefault(h, code)  # CAS: identical code dedups
    versions.append(h)
    return h

save('x = 1'); save('x = 1'); save('x = 2')
print('versions:', versions, '(3 saves, %d unique: dedup)' % len(store))
print('history with diffs; restore any; lesson steps for teaching')
